description: The words of the catch game, in 3D or flat: cards that rise over lanterns on an island one after another, each SAFE (the learner walks to it and catches it) or a HAZARD (the learner leaves it until its lantern goes out), while wordless chasers keep the learner moving. The same block as catch's, so a lecture switches the 2D and 3D look without touching its words. One card is one reported decision; its id is a data-question-id row on the page, and its outcome codes are that row's data-measures, never in here. Ask the person for every rule and source you were not given.

title.description: The game's title, on its first screen and its debrief.

items.description: The cards, in the order they appear. Mix safe and hazard; keep their labels about the same length, so the length never gives the answer away. Each card stays a few seconds over its lantern and has one outcome: caught (walked over) or passed (its lantern went out untouched).

id.description: The interaction id the LMS receives: ASCII, unique in the lecture, and the data-question-id of one row on the page. Take it from the client's alignment document; never invent it.

label.description: What the card says, read in a second while the learner moves: two to four words, a behaviour or a thing, never a verdict («آمن», «خطر») that tells the answer.

kind.description: safe: walking over it is right. hazard: letting its lantern go out is right, and catching it costs a heart. The response the LMS receives is caught or passed, and the result says whether that fits the kind.

rule.description: Why, in one sentence: shown after a wrong act during play, and in the debrief.

source.description: The citation the learner reads under the rule («المصدر: …»). Ask the person; never invent it. Left empty, the release lists it as left for the person.

slots.description: Optional: the art hand's own pictures for the game's four picture slots (game.json names their sizes), the same four as catch's. Each value is a path under the lecture's assets, such as "../assets/hero.png"; on the island a character's picture stands up facing the camera and the background tiles the ground. A slot left out keeps the game's own block-built model.

hero.description: The character the learner moves, seen from above or the front; transparent around it.

enemy.description: What chases the learner. It carries no words and stands for no answer; transparent around it.

item.description: The lantern every card stands over, the SAME for safe and hazard cards, so the picture never gives the answer away; transparent around it.

background.description: The ground, tiled over the island's blocks; opaque.
